title: Sub-floor steel bearers and bolt fixings in a SIP house built under a multiple-use approval
jurisdiction: New Zealand (MBIE Chief Executive determination; Building Act 2004; comparative only, not Alberta)
code_edition: NZ Building Code, First Schedule, Building Regulations 1992 (cited); B1 cited; edition not stated

facts.text: The consent was issued on 22 August 2018 for work described in a national multiple-use approval under section 30F; floors, walls and roof use 150 mm SIPs and the roof is a 15-degree gable.
The dispute is the on-site substitution of galvanised rolled steel bearers with a different profile from the consent, and the location of bolt fixings connecting the bearers to the timber.

Figure 1 shows the consented bearer profile and Figure 2 the installed profile (p.3); Figures 3 and 4 reproduce consent drawing details Dwg 406 (125 by 50 by 8 mm) and Dwg 401 (splice plate) (p.4); Figure 5 shows a proprietary splice plate (p.4).
